TESALONA Municipality of Lubang Occidental Mindoro Dear Vice-Mayor Tesalona: 2010 This has reference to your earlier letter asking the Department's legal opinion on the following issues, to wit: "1) Is an ordinance required to approve and operationalize MDC Resolution No. 003, Series •of • "2008? If so, what is the legal standing of'SB Resolution No. 63, series of 2008? e) Is it required that SB resolution NO. 63, series of "2008, assuming its validity, be förvvarded to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan ibr appropriate action? s) If,- in f.;tct, SB Resolution No. 63, series of 2008, should be _in ordinance förm, does its approval by the Sangguniang Panlala wigan make it valid? If SB Resolution No. 63, series of "2008 should be in ordinance iÖrm and if its approval by the Sangguniang Panlala wigan does not correct the legal infirmity of' SB Resolution No. 63, series of '2008, what is the current legal standing of said resolution? If,' in Fact, SB Resolution No. 63, Series of • '2008, has legal infirmity, can the '20% development plan covered under MDC Resolution No. 003, Series of'200S, be operationalized or implemented under the la WP'

-2- We shall answer all your queries in one discussion since they are interrelated. In reply thereto, please be informed that by statutory mandate, the formulation and initiation of the municipality's development plan is the primary function of the Municipal Development Council and the same has to be submitted to the Sangguniang Bayan for its appropriate action and approval pursuant to Section 109 (a) in relation to Section 114 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160). Such submission and approval are only for purposes of the enactment by the Sanggunian of the corresponding ordinance providing for legislative authorization of the budget for the proposed development projects consistent with the fundamental principle that no money shall be paid out of the local treasury except in pursuance of an appropriations ordinance [Section 305 (a), Ibid]. Be that as it may, may we invite your attention to the ruling of the Supreme Court, insofar as pertinent, in the case of Favis vs. City of Baguio, G.R. No. L-29910 (April 25, 1969), thus: "We first address ourselves to the preliminary questions raised in the appeal. I. Amongst these is appellant's charge that the resolutions directing the partial closing of Lapu-Lapu Street and the lease thereof are invalid. Because, so appellant avers, those resolutions contravene the City Charter. He relies on subsection (L) of Section 2553 of the Revised Administrative Code. It provides that the powers granted to the City— including the power to close streets—shall be carried "into effect by ordinance." This objection is directed at form, not at substance. It has been held that "even where the statute or municipal charter requires the municipality to act by ordinance, if a resolution is passed in the manner and with the statutory formality required in the enactment of an ordinance. it will be

-2- binding and effective as an ordinance." Such resolution may operate regardless of the name by which it is called. Resolutions No. 132 and 215, Series of 1961, were unanimously approved with all the councilors present and voting, carried the seal of the city council, were signed by the City Vice-Mayor, the Presiding Officer, approved by the City Mayor, and attested by the City Secretary. With the presumption of validity of the resolution and the other presumption that official duty has been regularly performed, the embattled resolutions are just as good as ordinances and have the same force. May we note that, upon perusal of the copy of Resolution No. 63, series of 2008, majority of all the Sangguniang Bayan Members had approved the same; you, as the Presiding Officer, actually certified the same to be duly adopted by the Sangguniang Bayan; the Secretary to the Sanggunian has duly attested the same; and the same was duly approved by the Mayor. In view thereof and taking into account the aforementioned ruling of the Supreme Court in the Favis case, SB Resolution No. 63, Series of 2008 is just as good as an ordinance and have the same force as such. Accordingly, SB Resolution No. 63, Series of 2008 should be subject to the review power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in accordance with Section 56 of the Local Government Code of 1991. We hope this finally settles your concern. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: JESUS B. Q V Director III Copy furnished: REGIONAL DIRECTOR ROLANDO B.
